links.outcome: Sensitivity for bacterial pharyngitis across models
links.effect: All models had high specificity (96-98%) but low sensitivity (2-15%) for bacterial pharyngitis, so negative results miss most bacterial cases and physician review is needed.
links.quote: The high specificity (96–98%) suggests strong potential for reducing unnecessary antibiotic prescriptions through AI-assisted triage, while the low sensitivity (2–15%) necessitates physician review for suspected bacterial infections.

unlisted_practices: Stratifying AI evaluation by physician consensus level (high vs low agreement) to reveal performance limits on ambiguous cases

screen.reason: The study develops an evaluation framework stratifying benchmark dataset performance by physician consensus to assess the diagnostic limits and safety profile of deep learning models for pharyngitis, but does not test an organizational deployment practice.
